html:
A Spanish conquistador, the chief lieutenant of Hernán Cortés in the conquest of the Aztecs and then the conqueror of much of Central America. He was known even among Spaniards for greed and cruelty.

In 1520, while Cortés was away, Alvarado led a massacre of Aztec nobles during a festival in the main temple of Tenochtitlan. The city rose up and drove the Spaniards out, before its final fall in 1521.

In 1523 Cortés sent him south with Spanish troops and thousands of Native allies. He beat the K'iche' in the highlands of Guatemala and burned their kings at their capital. He allied with the Kaqchikel against the Tz'utujil, then turned on the Kaqchikel with demands for gold, setting off years of revolt. He pushed on into El Salvador, against the Nahua-speaking Pipil. As governor of Guatemala he handed out land and Native labour to his men.

He sailed to Peru in 1534 hoping for a share of Inca wealth but was paid to leave. In 1541 he went to put down the Mixtón revolt of the Caxcan and others in western Mexico, and died after a horse fell on him.
sum: A Spanish conquistador, the chief lieutenant of Hernán Cortés in the conquest of the Aztecs and then the conqueror of much of Central America. He was known even among Spaniards for greed and cruelty.
